newsitem.title: UK: American backs Boeing after EU deal.
newsitem.headline: American backs Boeing after EU deal.

text.p: AMR Corp's American Airlines said on Wednesday Boeing Co's agreement with the European Union to drop its exclusive supply terms with American would make no practical difference to its decision to buy Boeing aircraft.
AMR made clear that it would continue to buy its aircraft from Boeing rather than European rival Airbus Industrie.
"American Airlines has said previously that it has no particular problem with Boeing ending the 'exclusivity' portion of our contract," the U.S. airline said in a statement released in London.
Boeing dropped the exclusivity terms in its long-term supply agreements with AMR, Delta Air Lines and Continental Airlines to appease European competition commissioner Karel Van Miert.
Van Miert had objected to Boeing's merger with McDonnell Douglas on the grounds that it would reduce competition in the civil aircraft market.

"The other elements of our recent aircraft order and contract with Boeing remain intact," AMR said. "American is quite satisfied with the fleet decisions we have made and the orders we have placed with Boeing," it said.
American said the current order with Boeing was for 98 aircraft with further purchase rights similar to options which would provide sufficient new aircraft "to meet our needs in the years ahead."
